definition.interpretation: The variance delta of 0.2285 meets the predicted threshold of >= 0.0004, supporting the initial divergence hypothesis. However, instrument reliability remains unvalidated, meaning this result reflects numerical model behaviour rather than confirmed structural divergence.
definition.limitations: Lack of independent measurement oracle; results are susceptible to internal model bias.
definition.next_step: Refine the hypothesis to account for the unvalidated instrument status and propose a more robust falsification criteria.

assumptions: Variance delta measurements are indicative of state divergence.
Observed divergence is not an artifact of pseudo-random generator initialization at 0.85 coupling.
definition.falsification: If the variance delta remains below 0.0004 in a replicated trial with isolated stochastic seeds, the hypothesis of path-dependent divergence is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling parameters are reduced to 0.85, resulting in a variance delta exceeding 0.0004; this effect persists even when controlling for model-side stochastic noise.
definition.uncertainty: Current measurement relies on an unvalidated instrument; observed divergence may be noise.

proposal.summary: Interpretation of recent divergence variance experiments (test-117) and refinement of the path-dependence hypothesis to accommodate unverified instrumentation.
proposal.title: WAKE Research: Interpretation of Path Dependence Experiments
